output.title: Measuring late payment terms without guessing
output.body:
If you want to measure late payment terms, keep the decision narrow: are you still tracking due dates, actual payment dates, and follow-up status by memory or spreadsheet, or do you already have a repeatable check that flags overdue invoices before they turn into a cash-flow surprise?

The useful first step is not a full finance redesign. It is a bounded workflow: compare the invoice date, agreed terms, and payment date; flag anything past due; and keep a simple log of what was late. Any collection action still stays with a human. Money movement stays human too.

If you are unsure whether this is worth automating, ask yourself: how many invoices do you issue each month, and how do you currently know which ones are late?

Then audit one week of invoices. Count which were paid on time, which were late, and how long the manual review took. That gives you a clean picture of the work before you decide whether a small automation pilot is worth doing. Dry, but useful.
